brief: A contacts app as a social constellation — closeness reflects relationship, interactions glow

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: ME node with radiating contacts evokes a real constellation, supported by a soft glow on the focal node.
Coherent dark palette with vivid contact hues that double as identity coding in both sidebar and graph map.
Detail card composition is clean — stat grid, hierarchy, and orange accent tie back to selected sidebar row.
dominant_weaknesses: Spatial encoding is weak — node distances don't visibly map to 'closeness' (95% Sarah sits as far as 'Acquaintance' Anna).
Connection lines are nearly invisible, undermining the constellation metaphor; no star-field, orbits, or weight differentiation.
Sidebar typography is generic system-stack and competes with the gradient logo; no shared typographic personality with the cosmic theme.
fix_priorities: Make distance and edge-weight semantic: pin closer contacts physically nearer ME with thicker/glowing links proportional to closeness%.
Add ambient star-field, orbital rings, or parallax to commit to the constellation metaphor instead of generic graph nodes.
Differentiate selected/unselected nodes with halo, scale, or pulse so interaction state reads instantly across the canvas.
Introduce a more characterful display typeface for headings and node labels to match the celestial concept.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral concept and reflective metaphor land well, but behavioral clarity suffers because the graph layout doesn't actually encode the data it claims to.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the constellation idea is legible and interactions glow subtly, but closeness is asserted in numbers rather than expressed in spatial geometry.
